Echoed literal: no. Expected values are either seeded data read back through production handles or override values echoed through the Engine's own `ok` line and file. Deleting the swap's `os.replace` turns 353 and 395 red. Deleting the worker's startup-build call turns 307, 334 and 356 red.\n4. One value: no. The opener is read at missing, no-table, empty and non-empty (free and held). The worker is read at startup_build False and True. Engines run with refresh on/interval 0, refresh off/interval 0, and refresh off/interval 0.25.\n5. The double: no owned module is replaced. `counting_build` and the runner's `gated_build` wrap the real `build_random_cache` and delegate to it. The SimpleNamespace owner is the owner contract the plan specifies for in-process tests (SimilarServer cannot be imported in pytest because of faiss), and the three Engine tests exercise the real SimilarServer.\n6. It collects: yes. `tests/last_test_output.txt` from the collect-only run shows \"10 tests collected\", and that still holds: the session test was replaced one for one by `test_refresh_off_engine_over_a_usable_cache_with_interval_0_starts_no_build`. The unused `engine` and `CHECKOUT_CACHE` imports are gone. The runs below imported and ran every test.\n7. Observed, not predicted: yes, now. I ran a probe (tests/tmp/test_probe_phase4_gate.py, since emptied) that patched `random_cache.build_random_cache` and called `refresh_random_cache`. It printed \"PROBE ok True calls 1 rows [1..20] names ['random-cache.db']\", which shows the gate's module-global patch is what the refresh path calls, and gives the worker test its expected rowids and directory contents. The mode-line shape {'mode': 'default', 'random_cache_refresh': 'false'}, the feed's row shape and whitelist lookups, and the held-lock control were all observed in the runs below. One limit: the `ok` line's post-phase token values (size, path) and the post-phase inode changes can only be seen once the phase exists. They rest on the `ok` format at random_cache.py:277, which already exists.\nRewrites made: (a) The session-Engine test failed its own control. The first run showed `AssertionError: [{'mode': 'default', 'random_cache_refresh': 'false'}]` at line 408, because the interval token and conftest's interval-0 env are phase-4 deliverables. It is replaced by a refresh-off variant Engine whose interval of 0 comes from the override, with the gate set. It asserts that nothing enters the gate, no start line appears, the inode and rows are unchanged and the feed is served from the seeded file, and its controls use only tokens observed today. (b) TICKS_WITHIN_SECONDS went from 150 to 90. Post-phase, three `ok` lines arrive in about 30 s (the startup build plus two 15 s ticks). The first full run hit the tool's 120 s cap (\"timed out after 120s\", exit 124), and 90 s lets the test be observed. (c) The seeding query was pulled out into `_seed_servable_cache`, which both gated tests now share.\n8. Red, not green: yes. The ValidateTests tool caps a run at 120 s and the whole file takes longer (exit 124), so I ran it in three selections that together cover all 10 tests. In-process: \"7 failed, 3 deselected\", exit 1. Refresh-on plus refresh-off: \"1 failed, 1 passed, 8 deselected\", exit 1. Positive interval: \"1 failed, 9 deselected\", exit 1. The refresh-off test passes before the phase, as expected: today's code already reuses a usable cache without building, and its assertions judge the phase's startup decision and are armed by the refresh-on sibling.\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. Lines 237 and 258 fail with \"AttributeError: module 'data.random_cache' has no attribute 'open_random_cache_if_usable'\", and line 292 fails with \"...has no attribute 'run_random_cache_worker'\". Both are functions this phase adds. In the held-lock case the control at 254 passed before the failure at 258. Line 334 (a claim assertion, not a control) fails with \"AssertionError: no build reached the gate within 30s of the Engine answering health\". The Engine did become healthy, but today it builds in place before listening and never through `build_random_cache`, and the probe showed the patched global is what the refresh path calls. Line 393 fails with \"AssertionError: 0 ok lines within 90s ... assert 0 >= 3\" after the feed loop ran for 90 s with no bad answer and no lookup failure, so the harness works and there is no background worker yet. No control failed in the final runs.\n10. Observed expected output: every row's `expected` matches what the runs showed wherever the current code reaches that line: the AttributeErrors at 237, 258 and 292; 334 red with the Engine healthy; 393 red at 0 `ok` lines; the refresh-off assertions at 423-429 green, with the mode line and feed shape as observed. The post-release values (349-356) and the tick values (395, 398-399) cannot be reached before the phase exists. They are the phase's own claims, and each row says where its value comes from.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:4": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/data/random_cache.py`\n- `refresh_random_cache` now logs `random cache build start target=\u2026 filtered=\u2026 max_per_instance=\u2026 max_per_author=\u2026 temp=\u2026` right before it calls `build_random_cache`. The plan had this line inside `build_random_cache`. The checkpoint's gate replaces `build_random_cache` and requires the start line to be in the log while the build is held at the gate, so the line has to come from the caller. Logging it in both places would give two start lines per Engine build, and the checkpoint allows exactly one. As a result the precompute job, which calls `build_random_cache` directly, logs no start line.\n- Added `open_random_cache_if_usable(path) -> Connection | None`:\n  - A missing file is checked with `path.exists()` first, so it is never created, and logs `reason=missing`.\n  - Otherwise the file is opened with `connect_readonly_db` (`mode=ro`) and counted with `random_rowids_count`.\n  - Any `sqlite3.Error` closes the handle, logs the error type and message, and returns None.\n  - A missing table or an empty table closes the handle, logs `reason=no_table` or `reason=empty`, and returns None.\n  - A non-empty cache returns the read-only handle. It only reads, so it opens even while another connection holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.\n- Added `run_random_cache_worker(source_path, active_path, size, filtered_mode, max_per_instance, max_per_author, owner, stop_event, startup_build, interval_seconds)`. It runs the startup build through `refresh_random_cache` if asked. Then, while `interval_seconds > 0`, it waits `stop_event.wait(interval_seconds)`, returns if the event is set, and otherwise builds again. With interval 0 it returns after at most the startup build. A failed build is logged by `refresh_random_cache` and retried at the next tick.\n- Left in place: `RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, its rat-tail comment, and the `reuse_non_empty` keyword with its branch in `populate_random_cache`. The Engine no longer uses them, but the already-gated tests in `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` still import and call them. Removing them before those tests are moved to `tests/archive/random_cache_in_place/` would break the active suite (see below).\n\n### `engine/server/api/server.py`\n- Imports:\n  - `from data.random_cache import open_random_cache_if_usable, run_random_cache_worker` replaces `connect_random_cache_db, populate_random_cache`.\n  - `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes` is added to the `server_config` import.\n- `random_cache_interval = random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes(args.dev)` is resolved next to `random_cache_refresh`. The function reads the module global when called, so the variant runner's override (including 0.25) gets through.\n- The in-place startup `connect_random_cache_db` + `populate_random_cache(..., reuse_non_empty=True)` block is replaced:\n  - `random_cache_db = open_random_cache_if_usable(random_cache_path)`\n  - `random_cache_startup_build = random_cache_refresh or random_cache_db is None`\n  - The `mkdir` stays, because the temp file is written in that directory.\n- Just before `serve_forever`, after `SimilarServer` exists, a daemon `threading.Thread` named `random-cache-refresh` runs `run_random_cache_worker`:\n  - Its arguments are `db_path`, `random_cache_path`, the size, filtered mode and cap constants, `server` as the owner, a `threading.Event`, the startup-build flag, and `random_cache_interval * 60` seconds.\n  - It starts only when a startup build is needed or the interval is above 0.\n- The `finally` block:\n  - sets the stop event first, with no join;\n  - closes whatever `server.random_cache_db` holds, taken and cleared under `server.random_cache_lock`, instead of the startup local.\n- Not changed here, because the plan's documentation list assigns them to the docs step: the `--dev` and refresh-flag help text, and the interval token on the `[similar-server] mode=` log line.\n\n### `tests/active/conftest.py`, `tests/active/test_random_cache.py`, `tests/archive/random_cache_in_place/test_random_cache_in_place.py`\nNot touched. This step covers production code only, and the checkpoint doesn't depend on any of these files. They still need to be done:\n- Move the four in-place tests into the archive file. They are the two busy-wait tests and the two `reuse_non_empty` tests. After that, `RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `reuse_non_empty` can be deleted from `random_cache.py`.\n- Reword the conftest and 8-Engine-test comments that describe in-place writes.\n- The plan's `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES=0` for the session Engine's environment is not set yet. Until it is, the session Engine and the 8 Engines each start an idle 60-minute worker. A suite run longer than an hour would do a full filtered build and rename it over the checkout's `random-cache.db`.\n\nNot verified:\n- I did not run the checkpoint or any probe. The workflow's run will be the first time this code is exercised.\n- The Engine tests read `random cache build \u2026` INFO lines from the log. The default `RECOMMENDATIONS_LOG_PROFILE` is `verbose`, which prints them. If the environment sets `focused`, those lines are dropped (this is unchanged since phase 2's `ok` line).\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "step_8_i1_refactor": "<refactors>\nengine/server/data/random_cache.py \u2014 reworded the rat-tail on RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (comment only). It used to say a longer Engine rebuild fails \"database is locked\" and named issues 22/23 as the fix. That fix has now landed: every build writes a per-pid temp file. The comment now says the wait only applies to a caller writing a shared cache file, and only the in-place tests still do that. The upgrade path it names is archiving those tests and dropping the timeout.\nengine/server/data/random_cache.py \u2014 reworded the rat-tail on the `reuse_non_empty` branch in populate_random_cache (comment only). It now says no production caller passes the flag, because the Engine opens its cache read-only; only the in-place tests use it, and it goes when they are archived.\n</refactors>\n\n<left_out>\nDeleting RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and the `reuse_non_empty` keyword and branch. The Engine and the job no longer use them. But the gated tests in tests/active/test_random_cache.py still call them: the busy_timeout test, the 6 s lock-wait test and the two refresh-off reuse tests. tests/archive/random_cache_in_place/test_random_cache_in_place.py does not exist. Phase 4 lists it as NEW, but its outcome says it was never written. Moving those tests changes the bytes of a gated file, which stops the build and goes to the operator. So that is your decision to make, and the deletion follows once it is done.\nDurable tests are missing. The phase 1\u20134 checkpoints (T1\u2013T14) still live only in tests/tmp/test_22_random_cache_background_refresh_phase{1..4}.py. Their planned homes are tests/active/test_random_cache.py and tests/active/test_server_config.py, and none of them were copied there. Adding tests is outside a production refactor pass.\ntests/active/conftest.py is out of date. Its comment still says the Engine \"waits on another writer's lock itself\". It also does not set RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES=0 in the session Engine's environment, so the session Engine and the 8-Engine test each start a 60-minute worker. A suite run longer than an hour would rename a full filtered build over the checkout's random-cache.db. The 8-Engine test's docstring also still describes in-place writes. Both are test files outside this pass; the missing env setting changes behaviour.\nStale help and log text is left to the docs step, as the plan assigns it: the DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH comment in server_config.py, the --dev and refresh-flag help in server.py, and the missing interval token on the `mode=` log line.\nSmall consolidations I skipped: the INSERT SQL duplicated in populate_random_cache, the count query after ensure_random_cache_schema that could use random_rowids_count, and the commit in build_random_cache that repeats populate's own. None of them simplifies anything, and the commit is a guard for the size<=0 path.\nThrowaway probes to delete: tests/tmp/probe_journal_memory_under_reserved.py and the other tests/tmp probes and checkpoints are still there, and I have no delete tool.\nThe step's \"What the pass is measured against\" section came through as the literal `{rat_tail_rules}` placeholder, so I measured this pass against the rat-tail rule in my role instead.\n</left_out>\n\n<needs_fresh_red>\nArchiving the in-place tests needs a fresh red before the dead production code can go, and it needs your go-ahead. The build process would move the four in-place tests out of the gated tests/active/test_random_cache.py and move the phase checkpoints into the active suite. Setting RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES=0 for the session Engine in conftest.py also needs a fresh red: it changes behaviour, which a refactor can't.\n</needs_fresh_red>\n\n<observation>\nThe production code from phases 1\u20134 was already tidy, so the only safe changes were two rat-tail comments that described the in-place rebuild. The dead timeout and `reuse_non_empty` code can't go until you retire the gated in-place tests. I ran nothing, and both edits are comment-only.\n</observation>",
    "step_9_triage": "<docs>\n<doc path=\"DATA_BUILD.md\" update=\"yes\">\n\u00a76, line 280, is now false on both counts. Its \"If a running Engine is rebuilding the cache, the job waits for that rebuild to finish, up to an hour\" sentence is wrong: the job now builds `<out-stem>.tmp.<pid>.db` beside the resolved `--out` and moves it into place with `os.replace`. It never writes `--out` in place and never waits on an Engine. The refresh-on sentence (\"a refresh-on start \u2026 rebuilds it towards `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_SIZE`\") must say that the Engine listens first and builds in a background worker. That happens at start when refresh is on or no usable cache exists (missing file, missing table or empty table), and then every `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`. Each build is swapped in atomically. Two more points to state: without `--reset` or `--refresh`, the job exits without writing when `--out` already holds at least `--size` rows, and `--reset` and `--refresh` both just skip that check. A running Engine keeps reading the file it opened until its own next build or a restart. The refresh-off reuse sentence stays true. Line 13 (optional): a leftover `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` or its `-journal` from a crashed build is safe to delete.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md\" update=\"yes\">\nRandom Cache Params, line 130: \"when true, rebuild the cache on every startup\" no longer describes the behaviour. `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH` now governs only the startup build. That build runs in the background after the Engine is listening, and until it swaps in, the existing cache (or the DB fallback) keeps serving. The refresh-off clause stays accurate, but \"builds one\" must say it builds in the background. Add a bullet for `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`: an environment variable read in `server_config.py`, a non-negative integer, default `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` = 60. When it is unset it is 0 under `--dev`, and an explicit value wins over `--dev`. 0 disables the periodic build. An invalid value exits at startup naming the variable. The refresh flags do not affect it. Add one sentence on the build: a temp file beside the cache, then a rename, then a read-only handle swapped in under `random_cache_lock`, with a failed build leaving the serving cache untouched. Lines 76 and 114, \"(or random from DB if cache is empty)\": the DB fallback also covers a missing cache, or one not usable at start, until the first background build swaps in.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md\" update=\"yes\">\n\u00a72 item 4, line 62: the refresh-off wording stays true, but the item says nothing about when builds happen, and the reader is left assuming a build before listening. Say that builds run in a background worker, at start (refresh on or no usable cache) and every `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, and are swapped in atomically. Also say that while no usable cache is open, random pools come from the DB. Align lines 78 and 94 (\"or random from DB if cache is empty\" / \"or random from DB\") with that: missing, not yet built, or empty.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DEPLOYMENT.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe document has no word on the new setting or on the Engine's in-process cache builds, and every production unit now runs them hourly. \u00a72, after the line-114 retention paragraph, in the same shape: `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` is set by an `Environment=` line in the Engine unit or in `.env.bridge`. It defaults to 60, 0 disables it, and the units run without `--dev`, so the default applies. Each build is a full filtered scan of `whitelist.db` in a background thread of the serving Engine, which costs CPU/GIL time that request threads compete for. Triage table (near line 160): add a row in the style of the retention row for `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES must be a non-negative integer, got '\u2026'`. The check runs at `server_config` import, so the DB jobs, the precompute job and the updater worker exit the same way. \u00a74 Run: `/api/health` answers before any random-cache build. Until the first `random cache build ok` line (or with no usable cache), the random feed is served from the DB. The `random cache build start/ok/failed` lines are INFO, so they appear only in the verbose log profile. A `failed` line leaves the previous cache serving, and the build is retried at the next tick. Optional: leftover `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` files are safe to delete.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/server.py\" update=\"yes\">\nThe report says the phase 4 implementer and the refactor pass left these for the docs step. The `--dev` help (about lines 159-162) must add that it also sets the periodic random-cache interval to 0 unless `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` is set. The `[similar-server] mode=` startup log line (about line 475) gains a `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes=%d` token in key=value form, from the resolved `random_cache_interval`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/server_config.py\" update=\"yes\">\nThe `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH` comment (about line 344, \"Rebuild random cache on startup even if it already meets size\") was deliberately left stale in phase 3. It must say that the constant governs only the startup build, which runs in the background after the Engine listens. The phase 3 report says the new interval constant, the env read, `_resolve_non_negative_int_env` with its exit WHY comment and `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes` already carry comments. Check them for concision against the file's style, and check that the resolver comment names the explicit-0-wins rule. Nothing else to add.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/data/db.py\" update=\"yes\">\nThe `connect_readonly_db` docstring (about lines 85-89) still describes only \"a second, read-only handle on the same database file\" for long statements. It now also opens the cache build's source scan, the random cache's serving handle (`open_random_cache_if_usable`), the precompute job's keep check, and the swap helper's validation handle. It must also warn that `mode=ro` on a missing file raises instead of creating it. `swap_readonly_connection` already has a full docstring from phase 2 (order, lock contract, never-`None`, temp-name journal caveat). Only review it for concision, and check that it states the handle keeps the temp name, so the caller's writes to that name must not use a disk rollback journal.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"scripts/worktree-setup.sh\" update=\"yes\">\nThe line 30 comment \"Rewritten by refresh-on starts and when missing or empty: private.\" is inaccurate. The file is now replaced by rename (never rewritten in place) at background startup builds and at every periodic build. It must stay a private `cp`, not a symlink, because the Engine resolves the path, so a symlink would put the temp file and the rename in main's `db/`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"tests/active/conftest.py\" update=\"yes\">\nThe engine fixture comment (lines 113-114) still says a start writes `random-cache.db` in place and \"waits on another writer's lock itself\". Now no start writes the cache before listening: builds go to a per-pid temp file in a background worker and are renamed in. Keep the `ENGINE_START_LOCK` explanation. This is a comment-only reword. Setting `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES=0` for the session Engine, which the refactor pass flagged, changes behaviour, is not a doc change and is the operator's call. This file is gated, so any byte change may need the operator's go-ahead.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"tests/active/test_random_cache.py\" update=\"yes\">\nThe 8-Engine test `test_engines_starting_at_once_all_become_healthy` explains itself through in-place writes and sqlite's busy wait: its docstring (about line 167), the control comments (172-175, 181-187) and the straggler comment (225-226). Each Engine now opens the cache read-only, needs no startup write, and becomes healthy before any build. Reword them to that. Scope limit on the module docstring: the four in-place tests (busy-wait, 6 s lock-wait, refresh-off reuse, missing/empty build) were not archived and are still in this file. Its bullets for them are therefore still true of the file, and only change if the operator retires those tests. The file is gated, so this edit needs the operator's go-ahead.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/22-random-cache-background-refresh.md\" update=\"yes\">\nDelivered. Set `Status: enhancement, complete`, add a closing comment and move the file to `docs/project/issues/archive/`. The comment names plan `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md` and the deltas from the issue text: a per-pid temp name `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` instead of `random-cache.tmp.db`; no WAL; a read-only serving handle; the validate-first `swap_readonly_connection` in `data/db.py`; and the hot-journal fix (a), `PRAGMA journal_mode=MEMORY` in `connect_random_cache_db`. It also names one daemon worker `run_random_cache_worker` with `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 60, 0 under `--dev` when unset).\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/23-random-cache-nonblocking-startup.md\" update=\"yes\">\nDelivered. Set `Status: enhancement, complete`, add a closing comment and move the file to archive. The comment says: the Engine opens a usable cache read-only, listens, and runs any startup build in the background, with the DB fallback serving until the first swap. It names the simplifications against lines 16-18: no backoff, no maximum build runtime, and no startup-mode setting (the refresh flags stand in for it). The comment must NOT say that the 3600 s `RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `reuse_non_empty` are retired. The checklist wording assumed it, but the delivered code still carries both. They are dead in production and used only by the in-place tests still in `tests/active/test_random_cache.py`, pending the operator's decision to archive those tests.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/plan.md\" update=\"yes\">\nMark lane 2d (line 72) delivered, and reword its note: the Engine no longer passes `reuse_non_empty` or uses the 3600 s wait, but both remain in `random_cache.py` until the in-place tests are archived. Lane 4b (line 91): point it at `swap_readonly_connection` in `engine/server/data/db.py` and its caveats. The installed handle keeps the temp name, so a later disk rollback journal at that name breaks reads (hence `journal_mode=MEMORY` on the temp writer). The helper also installs a read-only handle, while the similarity DB is written at serve time today.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/24-similarity-cache-shadow-swap.md\" update=\"yes\">\nLine 17 asks for a reopen of the similarity DB under `similarity_db_lock`. The generic helper now exists as `swap_readonly_connection(temp_path, target_path, lock, owner, attr, check_sql)` in `engine/server/data/db.py`. Add a comment pointing at it with its two cautions: the hot-journal trap of a handle carrying a temp name that a later build reuses, and the read-only handle versus today's serve-time writes to the similarity DB. Without it, lane 24 may repeat the defect.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/26-zero-downtime-deploy.md\" update=\"yes\">\nLine 30 names 23 as a prerequisite. Add a comment that 23 is delivered (with 22). Sibling Engines sharing a checkout stay on the old inode after another process's rename until their own next build or restart. That is the inode-check candidate the plan defers to 26.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/roadmap.md\" update=\"yes\">\nAdd a delivered entry after line 23 in the existing style, for issues `22`+`23`. It says the random cache builds in a background worker at start and every `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 60, 0 disables), is swapped in atomically through a temp file and a read-only handle, and that the Engine answers health without waiting on a build. It links `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md`. Mark 22 and 23 done in the line-156 chain `22 -> 23 -> 24/25 -> 26`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/plans/17-stable-ann-ids.md\" update=\"yes\">\nLine 33 (\"The random cache is rebuilt at start in production \u2026 `--dev` keeps a stored cache (`server.py:319-320`, `random_cache.py:43-45`)\") is now false. The Engine never writes the cache before listening, and those line references are stale. Line 105 assumes `ensure_random_cache_schema` repopulates an old-shape table at Engine start. That write no longer happens: under refresh off, an old-shape but non-empty table passes `open_random_cache_if_usable` and is served as is. Add a note that old-shape detection belongs in `open_random_cache_if_usable` (treat it as unusable, which triggers a background build) or in `build_random_cache`.\n</doc>\n</docs>\n\n<adr_conflicts>\nnone. I checked ADR-0006 (derived ANN ids), the only ADR that mentions the random cache: it covers the id the cache stores, not how it is built or swapped. No other ADR touches this area. The inventory's optional new ADR (temp build, rename and read-only handle swap, no WAL, for reuse by issue 24) is not a conflict. It is left to the operator.\n</adr_conflicts>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DATA_BUILD.md": "<changes>\nDATA_BUILD.md \u00a76 now describes the temp-file-and-rename job and the Engine's background builds. The claim that the job waits up to an hour is gone.\n\n- **Job paragraph:** the job builds `<out-stem>.tmp.<pid>.db` beside the resolved `--out` and moves it into place with `os.replace`. It never writes `--out` in place and never waits on an Engine.\n  - Without `--reset`/`--refresh` it exits without writing when `--out` already holds at least `--size` rows. Those two flags both just skip that check.\n  - A failed build removes its temp file. A leftover `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` or `-journal` from a killed process is safe to delete. I put this here rather than in the Outputs list at line 13.\n  - Checked against `precompute-random-rowids.py` and `build_random_cache`.\n- **Engine paragraph:** the Engine builds in a background worker after it starts listening.\n  - It builds at start when refresh is on or no usable cache exists (missing file, missing table or empty table), then every `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`. Each build targets `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_SIZE` and is swapped in atomically.\n  - A refresh-off start serves any non-empty cache as it is, including the job's 5000-row one, until its first periodic build.\n  - A running Engine keeps its opened file until its own next build or a restart.\n  - Checked against `server.py` lines 308\u2013334 and 477\u2013492, and `open_random_cache_if_usable`.\n- **Pointer:** the details of the interval and refresh settings are left to `LAYER_PARAMS.md`, which this section points to.\n\nTwo things I added beyond the checklist:\n- The phrase \"until its first periodic build\" is new. Under `--no-random-cache-refresh` without `--dev`, the 60-minute default still applies, so the Engine replaces the job's cache after an hour.\n- The step's \"How the writing is judged\" section came through as unfilled `{writing_*}` placeholders, so I wrote to the rules in my role instead.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md": "<changes>\nI updated LAYER_PARAMS.md to say random-cache builds run in the background, added the interval setting, and changed the DB fallback wording to match.\n\n- **`DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH` entry:** it now governs only the startup build. That build runs in the background once the Engine is listening, and the existing cache keeps serving until the new one swaps in. When refresh is off, the Engine builds in the background only if the cache is missing, has no `random_rowids` table, or is empty.\n- **New `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` entry:** it's an environment variable read in `server_config.py`. It must be a non-negative integer, and 0 turns it off. If it's unset, it's `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (60), or 0 under `--dev`. A value you set explicitly overrides `--dev`. An invalid value stops the Engine at startup with a message naming the variable. The refresh flags don't change it.\n- **New paragraph under Random Cache Params:** a build writes a temp file beside the cache, renames it over the cache, and swaps in a read-only handle under `random_cache_lock`. A failed build leaves the serving cache untouched. While no usable cache is open (missing, no table, empty, or not built yet), the random pool comes from the DB.\n- **explore and random layer \"Source:\" lines:** \"if cache is empty\" now reads \"while no usable cache is open\", with a link to Random Cache Params.\n\nI checked these against the code:\n- `server_config.py`: `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes`, which uses an `is not None` test so an explicit value wins.\n- `server.py`: the interval depends only on `args.dev`, and the worker starts when a startup build is needed or the interval is above 0.\n- `random_cache.py`: `open_random_cache_if_usable` and its missing / no_table / empty / sqlite-error reasons, and `refresh_random_cache`, which swaps under `owner.random_cache_lock`.\n- `random_videos.py`: the fallback when `server.random_cache_db is None`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md": "<changes>\nOVERVIEW.md: \u00a72 item 4 now covers when the random cache is built (background worker, at start and on an interval) and the DB fallback; the explore and random source lines say when the DB is used.\n\n- **\u00a72 item 4 (Random cache):**\n  - The Engine starts listening before any build and opens a usable cache read-only.\n  - One background worker builds a cache at start when refresh is on or there is no usable cache (missing file, missing or empty table, or a file that can't be read). The same worker rebuilds every `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`.\n  - The refresh-off sentence still says a non-empty cache is reused as it is.\n  - Each build is written to a temp file and swapped in atomically, and a failed build leaves the serving cache as it was.\n  - While no usable cache is open, random pools come from the DB.\n  - Defaults and build steps are left to `LAYER_PARAMS.md` \"Random Cache Params\", with a pointer to it.\n- **\u00a73 explore and random layers:** the source line now reads \"random cache (or random from DB while the cache is missing, not yet built or empty)\".\n\nI checked these against the code:\n- `server.py` 308\u2013334 and 477\u2013492: startup-build flag, interval, and the worker starting after the server exists.\n- `open_random_cache_if_usable` and `refresh_random_cache` in `random_cache.py`.\n- `fetch_random_rows_from_cache`: it returns `[]` when `random_cache_db` is None.\n- The `[]` \u2192 `fetch_random_rows` fallback in `candidates/random_videos.py` and `handlers/similar.py`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DEPLOYMENT.md": "<changes>\nDEPLOYMENT.md now documents `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, adds a triage row for a bad value, and explains how the Engine serves while random-cache builds run.\n\n- **\u00a72, after the retention paragraph:** a new paragraph in the same shape.\n  - It is set by an `Environment=` line in the Engine unit or in `.env.bridge`. It defaults to 60 and 0 disables it.\n  - Both contours' units run without `--dev` (checked against `ExecStart` in `engine/install-engine-service.sh`), so both use the default.\n  - Each rebuild is a full filtered scan of `whitelist.db` in a background thread of the serving Engine, so it takes CPU and GIL time from request threads. `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_FILTERED_MODE = True`.\n  - It points to `LAYER_PARAMS.md` for what the setting and the startup build do, rather than restating that here, and says a bad value stops the Engine at startup.\n- **Triage table:** a new row in the style of the retention row, for `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES must be a non-negative integer, got '\u2026'`. The example values are `abc`, `-3` and `7.5`. An empty value is left out because a blank value resolves to the default and is not an error. The row says the DB jobs, `precompute-random-rowids.py` and the updater worker exit the same way, because the check runs when `server_config` is imported.\n- **\u00a74 Run, after the health poll:**\n  - `/api/health` answers without waiting on any build.\n  - The random feed is served from `whitelist.db` until the first `random cache build ok` line, and whenever no usable cache is open.\n  - Each build logs `start`, then `ok` or `failed`. A `failed` line leaves the previous cache serving, and the build is retried at the next interval.\n  - Leftover `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` files are safe to delete.\n  - The log-line wording differs from the checklist. The checklist said these lines \"appear only in the verbose profile\". `logging_profiles.py` actually writes every record and only tags these INFO lines `modes: [\"verbose\"]`. So the text says they are tagged for the `verbose` view only, and that a viewer filtered to `focused` hides them.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/server.py": "<changes>\nI updated the `--dev` help, the two refresh-flag help texts and the `[similar-server] mode=` startup log line in `engine/server/api/server.py`. Nothing was run.\n\n- **`--dev` help:** it said \"disable random cache refresh\". It now says `--dev` skips the startup build when a usable cache exists (unless a refresh flag is given). It also says `--dev` sets the periodic interval to 0 unless `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` is set. I checked this against `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes` in `server_config.py` (lines 367-372).\n- **`--random-cache-refresh` help:** it now says the flag runs a background startup build after the server is listening, and does not affect the periodic build.\n- **`--no-random-cache-refresh` help:** it now says the flag skips the startup build when a usable cache exists, and does not affect the periodic build. A missing or empty cache is still built, following `random_cache_startup_build = random_cache_refresh or random_cache_db is None`.\n- **`mode=` log line:** it now ends with `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes=<value>`, taken from the resolved `random_cache_interval`. I used `%s` instead of the checklist's `%d`. The phase 4 report says the variant runner can set the interval to a fraction such as 0.25, which `%d` would print as `0`. That would make it look like the periodic build is off when it is running.\n\nI left the two existing WHY comments near the worker (the start-after-`server` note and the not-joined note) unchanged; they are still accurate.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/server_config.py": "<changes>\n`server_config.py`: the `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH` comment now describes the startup build as it works today, and the interval resolver's comment now says an explicit value wins over `--dev`.\n\n- **`DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH` (line 359):** the old comment was \"Rebuild random cache on startup even if it already meets size\". It now reads: \"Run a startup random cache build even when a usable cache exists. The build runs in the background after the Engine listens; this does not govern the periodic rebuilds.\" I checked this against `server.py`. Lines 316\u2013320 use the flag only to decide the startup build. Line 342 sets the startup build to \"refresh on, or no usable cache\". The interval is resolved separately, through `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes`.\n- **Comment in `random_cache_refresh_interval_minutes`:** it said only that an explicit 0 wins over \"the default\". It now says an explicit value, 0 included, must win over `--dev` and the default.\n- **Reviewed and left as they were:** the `_resolve_non_negative_int_env` docstring and its comment on why it exits, the `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` comment, the comment on the env read, and the resolver's docstring. They are short, accurate and in the file's style.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/data/db.py": "<changes>\nReworded the `connect_readonly_db` docstring to cover what it is used for now, and added a warning that `mode=ro` raises on a missing file.\n\n- **Before:** the docstring described it only as \"a second, read-only handle on the same database file\" for long statements.\n- **Now:** it says the function opens a read-only handle, with the deadline handler installed, on an existing database file. It is used wherever a read must not share a writer's handle or lock: long route statements, a cache build's scan of the source database, and serving handles on files that are never written in place.\n- **New warning:** `mode=ro` never creates the file. A missing path raises `sqlite3.OperationalError`, so callers that expect the file might be absent should check first.\n- **Checked against the code:** I grepped the callers: `server.py:331` (search), `random_cache.py:230` (the build's source scan), `random_cache.py:291` (`open_random_cache_if_usable`), `precompute-random-rowids.py:67` (the keep check) and `db.py:121` (the swap helper). The docstring describes these by role rather than listing them.\n- **`swap_readonly_connection` docstring:** I reviewed it and left it as it is. It is concise enough, and it already says the handle's journal name is fixed at open as `<temp_path>-journal`. So it already warns that later writes to that name must not use a disk rollback journal.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:scripts/worktree-setup.sh": "<changes>\nReworded the `random-cache.db` comment in `scripts/worktree-setup.sh`: every build replaces the file by rename, and it has to stay a private copy rather than a symlink.\n\n- Line 30 was `# Rewritten by refresh-on starts and when missing or empty: private.` It now reads `# Replaced by rename at every Engine cache build, startup and periodic: a private copy, not a symlink, because the Engine resolves the path and would build and rename into main's db/.`\n- I checked the comment against the code:\n  - `server.py:328` resolves the path with `(repo_root / DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_DB_PATH).resolve()`, which follows symlinks.\n  - `random_cache.py:197-199` puts the temp file beside the resolved path (`active_path.with_name(...)`).\n  - So a symlinked copy would have its temp file and rename land in main's `db/`.\n- The `cp` line itself is unchanged.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:tests/active/conftest.py": "<changes>\nReworded the `engine` fixture comment in `tests/active/conftest.py`: an Engine start no longer writes `random-cache.db` in place or waits on a lock.     "step_9_i2_update:tests/active/test_random_cache.py": "<changes>\nReworded the 8-Engine test's docstring, comments and one assert message so they describe the read-only startup open instead of in-place writes. Comments and one message string only; no test logic changed. The operator approved the change to this gated file.\n\n- **Docstring, second paragraph:** each Engine opens the non-empty cache read-only, which the held write lock doesn't block. With refresh off it runs no startup build, so it starts listening without writing the cache. A start that did write the cache would wait on the lock and never become healthy. The launch command and environment sentence and the session-fixture sentence are unchanged.\n- **Non-empty control comment:** a non-empty cache is usable, so a refresh-off start serves it and runs no startup build.\n- **Short-cache control comment and its assert message:** a start that filled the cache towards its size would write a short cache and leave a full one alone. So only a short cache shows that a start never writes it. The assert message now says \"a start that fills it towards size\" instead of \"a start without reuse\".\n- **Lock control comment:** a start that writes the active cache file waits on the lock instead of becoming healthy.\n- **Straggler comment:** an Engine blocked in sqlite on the held lock ignores SIGTERM until the call returns, so a straggler is killed at the deadline. The busy-wait framing is gone.\n- **Checked against the code:** `open_random_cache_if_usable` in `data/random_cache.py` opens the file with `connect_readonly_db` and returns the handle when it has rows. In `server.py`, `random_cache_startup_build = random_cache_refresh or random_cache_db is None`, and the worker thread is started just before `serve_forever`.\n- **Left as it is:** the module docstring. Its first four bullets describe the four in-place tests, which are still in this file. The fifth bullet (8 Engines, write lock held, healthy within 120 s) is still accurate. Those bullets only change if the operator archives the in-place tests.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/22-random-cache-background-refresh.md": "<changes>\nIssue 22 closed as delivered: `Status: enhancement, complete`, a `### Delivered` comment added, and the file written to `docs/project/issues/archive/22-random-cache-background-refresh.md`. **The original `docs/project/issues/22-random-cache-background-refresh.md` still has to be deleted.** I have no tool that deletes files.\n\n- The issue body is unchanged. The only edits are the Status line and the new comment.\n- The comment follows the format of the existing archived issues (see `archive/17-feed-modes.md`). It names plan `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md` and says 23 was delivered with it. The commit is written as `<pending>`, as in that precedent.\n- The comment covers what was delivered and where it differs from the issue text:\n  - **Worker:** one daemon thread, `run_random_cache_worker`. It runs the startup build if one is needed, then a build every N minutes. A failed build is retried at the next tick, and shutdown does not wait for a build in progress.\n  - **Interval:** `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` defaults to 60, or to 0 under `--dev` when it is unset. An explicit value, 0 included, wins over `--dev`, and the refresh flags do not affect it.\n  - **Temp file:** each build writes `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` instead of `random-cache.tmp.db`, so Engines sharing a checkout never write the same file.\n  - **SQLite:** no WAL. The cache is served through a read-only `mode=ro` handle.\n  - **Swap:** `swap_readonly_connection` in `data/db.py` checks the new file before renaming it into place, and has nothing random-cache-specific in its interface, so issue 24 can reuse it.\n  - **Hot-journal fix (a):** `PRAGMA journal_mode=MEMORY` in `connect_random_cache_db`.\n  - **Logs:** the `start`/`ok`/`failed` lines, plus the existing lines in `populate_random_cache` for rows scanned and a short fill.\n- Settings, operations and the precompute job are covered by pointers to `LAYER_PARAMS.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` and `DATA_BUILD.md` rather than repeated here.\n- I checked the facts against the code: `random_cache.py` (worker, refresh, the pragma, temp path, log lines), `server_config.py` (the default of 60 and the rule that an explicit value wins even when it is 0), and `db.py` (the swap order, `mode=ro`, no WAL anywhere in `data/`).\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\ndocs/project/issues/22-random-cache-background-refresh.md: this should be deleted, because the issue has moved to archive/. The archive copy is written, but I have no tool that deletes files, so both copies exist until someone removes this one.\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/23-random-cache-nonblocking-startup.md": "<changes>\nIssue 23 is closed as delivered: status set to `enhancement, complete`, a `### Delivered` comment added, and the file written to `docs/project/issues/archive/23-random-cache-nonblocking-startup.md`. **The original `docs/project/issues/23-random-cache-nonblocking-startup.md` still needs deleting, because I have no delete tool.**\n\n- **Status line:** `Status: enhancement, complete`.\n- **Delivered comment:** it follows the same layout as the archived issue 22 comment. It names the plan `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md` and says 22 was delivered with it. The commit is written as `<pending>` to match 22.\n  - **Startup:** the Engine opens the cache with `open_random_cache_if_usable`, which returns a read-only handle only when `random_rowids` exists and holds rows. It then listens without building. The startup build runs in the background worker `run_random_cache_worker`: always when refresh is on, and when refresh is off only if no usable cache was opened. I checked this against `connect_readonly_db` in `data/db.py`. So the waits listed in the issue-32 comment no longer happen.\n  - **The comment does not say** that `RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` or `reuse_non_empty` are retired.     "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/plan.md": "<changes>\nplan.md: lane 2d is marked delivered with its note reworded, and lane 4b now points at `swap_readonly_connection` and its two caveats.\n\n- **Lane 2d (line 72):** marked delivered, with a link to `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md`. The note now says the Engine no longer passes `reuse_non_empty` or relies on the 3600 s `RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` wait. Both still sit in `data/random_cache.py` until the in-place tests in `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` are archived. I checked this against the code: `server.py` has no `reuse_non_empty` call, and `random_cache.py` still defines the constant and the keyword.\n- **Lane 4b (line 91):** marks its dependency 23 as delivered. It tells the lane to reuse `swap_readonly_connection` in `engine/server/data/db.py` for the reopen, and names the two caveats:\n  - The installed handle keeps the temp name, so a later disk rollback journal at that name breaks its reads. This is why the random cache temp file uses `journal_mode=MEMORY`.\n  - The helper installs a read-only handle, but the Engine writes the similarity DB at serve time today. I confirmed this in `_write_cache` in `data/similarity_candidates.py`.\n- Nothing else in the file changed.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/24-similarity-cache-shadow-swap.md": "<changes>\nIssue 24: added a comment that points at `swap_readonly_connection` as the swap/reopen helper, with its two cautions.\n\nThe comment goes under `## Comments` as `### Swap helper from issue 22`. The rest of the issue is unchanged, including its `needs-triage` status.\n\n- **What the helper does.** It names `swap_readonly_connection(temp_path, target_path, lock, owner, attr, check_sql)` in `engine/server/data/db.py`, which the random cache uses through `refresh_random_cache`. In order, it:\n  - opens the finished file read-only;\n  - runs `check_sql`;\n  - calls `os.replace` onto the target;\n  - swaps the handle in under `lock`;\n  - closes the old handle once the lock is released.\n\n  If the open, the check or the rename fails, the target file and the handle are left as they were.\n- **No previous file.** The helper keeps no copy of the old cache, so the issue's `similarity-cache.prev.db` would be a copy the caller makes before the swap.\n- **Caution: hot journal.** The installed handle keeps the temp file's name. Every build would reuse the fixed name `similarity-cache.next.db`, and a disk rollback journal at that name makes every read fail. So the shadow build needs an in-memory journal (the way `connect_random_cache_db` sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=MEMORY`) or a temp name that is never reused.\n- **Caution: read-only handle.** The helper installs a `mode=ro` handle. But the Engine writes to the similarity DB while serving: `_write_cache` in `engine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py` writes through `server.similarity_db`, which `connect_similarity_db` opens read-write. Either those writes move elsewhere, or the helper needs a way to open read-write.\n\nI checked each claim against the code: the docstring and body of `swap_readonly_connection`, the comment on the pragma in `connect_random_cache_db`, `_write_cache` and `connect_similarity_db`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/26-zero-downtime-deploy.md": "<changes>\nAdded a comment to issue 26 saying prerequisite 23 is delivered (with 22), plus three effects on a blue/green pair that shares one checkout.\n\nThe comment is under `## Comments`, headed \"Prerequisite 23 delivered, with 22\":\n- **What was delivered:** it names plan `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md`. An Engine opens a usable `random-cache.db` read-only, starts listening, and runs every build in a background worker that renames the result over the active file. So a green `/api/health` does not mean a build has finished.\n- **Sibling Engines stay on the old inode:** after another Engine renames a new build into place, a sibling keeps reading the old file until its own next build or a restart. The plan left a per-request inode check for this issue to decide.\n- **Both ports build:** in production refresh is on and the units run without `--dev`. So each Engine runs its own startup build and its own build every `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, and two full scans of `whitelist.db` can overlap. Each Engine writes its own `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db`, so they never share a temp file.\n- **Stopping mid-build leaves a temp file:** the worker is a daemon thread and shutdown doesn't wait for it (`server.py` sets the stop event and doesn't join). Stopping the old instance during a build therefore leaves its `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db` behind, and it is safe to delete.\n\nChecked against the code in `engine/server/api/server.py`: the worker starts just before `serve_forever`, it starts only when a startup build is needed or the interval is above 0, and the `finally` block sets the stop event without joining.\n\nI did not change the Status line or the Related line. The issue is still open, and \"After `23-\u2026`\" is still an accurate ordering.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/roadmap.md": "<changes>\nAdded a Delivered entry for issues `22` and `23` and marked both as delivered in the runtime-reliability order.\n\n- **Delivered:** a new bullet after the issue `17` entry, written like the other entries. It says:\n  - The Engine answers `/api/health` without waiting on a random-cache build.\n  - It opens a usable cache read-only, starts listening, and does all building in one background worker, at start and every `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (60 by default, 0 disables).\n  - Each build goes to a temp file, is renamed over the cache, and is swapped in as a new read-only handle.\n  - The bullet points to `LAYER_PARAMS.md` \"Random Cache Params (Global)\" for the setting's details (the `--dev` default, the rule that an explicit value wins, the exit on an invalid value) and doesn't repeat them. It links `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md`.\n- **Implementation order:** the chain now reads `` `22` -> `23` (both delivered) -> `24`/`25` -> `26` ``.\n- **Checked against the code and repo:** the default of 60 is at `server_config.py:362`; `run_random_cache_worker` and `swap_readonly_connection` exist; the plan file exists; the `LAYER_PARAMS.md` heading is spelled exactly as linked.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/plans/17-stable-ann-ids.md": "<changes>\nPlan 17 updated: its current-code description of the random cache is correct again, and the plan for detecting an old-shape cache has moved to `open_random_cache_if_usable` and the precompute job's keep check.\n\n- **Line 33 (\"What the current code does\").** Replaced the false \"rebuilt at start in production / `--dev` keeps a stored cache\" line and its out-of-date line references. The new text, checked against the code:\n  - The Engine never writes the cache before it starts listening.\n  - At start it opens the cache read-only through `open_random_cache_if_usable` (`random_cache.py:283-302`). That function accepts any non-empty `random_rowids` table and does not check its shape.\n  - Every build runs through `build_random_cache` (`random_cache.py:208-245`) into a per-pid temp file. The background worker renames that file over the cache and swaps it in.\n  - With refresh off (`--dev`, `server.py:316-319`), a stored non-empty cache is served as it is.\n  - `precompute-random-rowids.py` keeps an `--out` that already holds `--size` rows. It counts them through `random_rowids_count` and does not check their shape.\n  - When builds run is not repeated here. The line points at `LAYER_PARAMS.md`, which owns the refresh and interval settings.\n- **P3 random-cache bullet.** Dropped the claim that `ensure_random_cache_schema` detects and repopulates an old table. That function now runs only on a build's fresh temp file, so it never sees a stored table. The bullet now says:\n  - Old-shape detection goes in `open_random_cache_if_usable`. It treats an old table as unusable, so the Engine serves from the DB and runs a background build.\n  - The precompute job's keep check must also treat an old-shape `--out` as not kept. The keep check was not on the checklist; I found it while checking the code.\n- **Not done as the checklist asked.** The checklist offered `build_random_cache` as a second place for the detection. I did not take it: that function never reads the stored file, so it cannot detect an old one. The bullet says this in one sentence.\n- AC6's requirement wording (\"detected and repopulated, not read\") is unchanged, since it is the settled requirement.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_10_plan": "<harvest_file>\ndocs/project/plans/harvest-22-random-cache-background-refresh-plan.md\n</harvest_file>\n\n<plan>\n## Harvest plan: issue 22 random cache background refresh\n\nScope: the 4 files this build wrote in `tests/tmp`, `test_22_random_cache_background_refresh_phase{1..4}.py`. The full classification, with a reason for each test, is in `docs/project/plans/harvest-22-random-cache-background-refresh-plan.md`.\n\n### Counts (19 test functions)\n\n| Verdict | Count |\n|---|---|\n| DURABLE | 17 |\n| REPLACES | 2 |\n| COMBINE | 0 |\n| REDUNDANT | 0 |\n| SPENT | 0 |\n\n### DURABLE \u2192 `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` (10)\n\n- phase 1: `test_build_writes_a_complete_cache_into_the_pid_temp_file_only`\n- phase 1: `test_build_failure_removes_the_temp_file_and_leaves_the_active_file`\n- phase 2: `test_refresh_serves_a_new_readonly_handle_on_the_renamed_file_and_closes_the_old`\n- phase 2: `test_second_same_pid_build_leaves_the_served_handle_readable` (the only gate on `journal_mode=MEMORY`)\n- phase 2: `test_readers_under_the_lock_never_fail_or_come_back_empty_across_refresh_cycles`\n- phase 2: `test_refresh_failure_keeps_the_active_file_and_the_handle_and_removes_the_temp_file`\n- phase 2: `test_stop_set_before_the_swap_keeps_the_active_file_and_the_handle_and_removes_the_temp_file`\n- phase 4: `test_worker_with_interval_0_returns_after_at_most_the_startup_build`\n- phase 4: `test_refresh_on_engine_serves_its_usable_cache_while_the_startup_build_is_held_then_swaps_in_200_rows`\n- phase 4: `test_positive_interval_swaps_a_new_file_in_each_tick_while_the_random_feed_serves_the_current_one`\n- phase 4: `test_refresh_off_engine_over_a_usable_cache_with_interval_0_starts_no_build`\n\nThat list is 11 tests. The 17 DURABLE tests are these 11 plus the 2 for `test_precompute_random_rowids.py`, the 1 for `test_db.py` and the 3 for `test_server_config.py`.\n\nThe helpers these tests need come with them: `_seed_cache`, `_cache_rows`/`_cache_rowids`, `_seeded`, `_refresh`, `_served_rowids`, `_names`, `_seed_servable_cache`, `_payloads`/`_messages`/`_tokens`/`_has_started`, `_feed_rowids`, `_cache_variant`, `CACHE_VARIANT_RUNNER` and their constants. The file's existing `_source_db` is reused; the phase-4 worker test closes the connection it returns. `ENGINE_START_LOCK` and `WHITELIST_DB` are added to the conftest import.\n\n### DURABLE \u2192 other subject files\n\n- `tests/active/test_precompute_random_rowids.py` (**new file**): phase 1 `test_job_builds_a_fresh_out_and_keeps_one_at_size` and `test_job_replaces_out_by_rename`, with `_source_db`, `_seed_cache`, `_cache_rows`, `_run_job` and `PRECOMPUTE_JOB`.\n- `tests/active/test_db.py`: phase 2 `test_swap_failure_leaves_the_target_and_the_handle_and_keeps_the_temp_file`. It calls `data.db.swap_readonly_connection` directly. Its fixtures come with it (`_source_db`, `_seed_cache`, `_names`, `_served_rowids`, the constants it uses), plus the `engine/server/api` sys.path entry that `data.random_cache` needs.\n- `tests/active/test_server_config.py`: phase 3 `test_unset_or_blank_gives_none_and_a_non_negative_integer_becomes_the_constant`, `test_a_value_that_is_not_a_non_negative_integer_stops_the_import` and `test_interval_is_the_env_value_when_set_else_0_under_dev_and_60_without`. They reuse the existing `_run(..., var)` and `_last_stderr_line`, with a new `INTERVAL_VAR`, `PRINT_INTERVAL` and `PRINT_RESOLVED`.\n\n### REPLACES \u2192 `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` (2)\n\n- phase 4 `test_a_missing_tableless_or_empty_cache_is_not_usable` replaces active `test_refresh_off_builds_a_missing_or_empty_cache`.\n  - The old test drives the `populate_random_cache(..., reuse_non_empty=True)` branch, which no production caller uses any more.\n  - The Engine now makes this decision in `open_random_cache_if_usable`, and the new test drives that function.\n- phase 4 `test_a_non_empty_cache_opens_read_only_even_under_a_held_write_lock` replaces active `test_refresh_off_reuses_a_short_cache_without_writing`.\n  - The rule is the same: serve a non-empty cache under a held write lock without writing to it.\n  - It is now enforced by a `mode=ro` open instead of the dead reuse branch.\n\n### Active tests to be retired\n\nThese two functions are cut from `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` into `tests/archive/random_cache_in_place/test_random_cache.py`, with the imports, `_source_db`, `SOURCE_ROWS` and `SEEDED_ROWS` they use:\n\n- `test_refresh_off_reuses_a_short_cache_without_writing`\n- `test_refresh_off_builds_a_missing_or_empty_cache`\n\n`test_random_cache.py` keeps three tests, so it is not moved whole.   "requirements": "### Purpose\n\nThe random feed is served from `engine/server/db/random-cache.db`. Today the cache is built in place, and only on startup: before the Engine listens, under the refresh-on default, or when the cache is missing or empty. This build (issues 22 and 23 together, as `docs/project/issues/plan.md` lane 2d directs) makes the cache refresh while the Engine keeps serving. There is no startup delay, no request is blocked or failed by a rebuild, and no rebuild runs on the request path. It is a prerequisite for `26-zero-downtime-deploy`, and its swap/reopen primitive is meant to be reused by `24-similarity-cache-shadow-swap`.\n\n### Scope decision (operator)\n\n- 22 (periodic background refresh) and 23 (non-blocking startup) are delivered as one build.\n- The plan file is `docs/project/plans/19-22-random-cache-background-refresh.md`.\n- When 22 is delivered, 23 is delivered with it.\n\n### One build path\n\n- Every cache build the Engine runs, at startup and periodically, uses one path:\n  - It scans the source through its own read-only connection to `whitelist.db`. It never uses `server.db` or `server.db_lock`, so a build blocks no request.\n  - It computes the full candidate list with the existing `populate_random_cache` logic: same size target, filtered mode, per-instance cap and per-author cap.\n  - It writes the result into a per-process temp file in the same directory as the active cache, `random-cache.tmp.<pid>.db`, commits it and closes it.\n  - It then moves the temp file onto `random-cache.db` with `os.replace` (atomic rename).\n- A per-process temp name is used instead of the fixed `random-cache.tmp.db`, because several Engines can share one checkout (the test harness starts one per lane) and must never write the same temp file.\n- After this build, the active cache file is never written in place.\n\n### Swap and reopen\n\n- After a successful replace, the Engine opens a new read-only connection to the new `random-cache.db`.\n- Under `server.random_cache_lock` it swaps that connection into `server.random_cache_db`. Only after the swap does it close the old connection.\n- `random_cache_lock` is held only for the reference swap, never during the build.\n- The swap/reopen helper takes a path, a lock and the owner/attribute to update, and has nothing random-cache-specific in its interface, so issue 24 can reuse it for the similarity cache.\n- Another Engine process sharing the checkout keeps reading the file it opened, which is the old inode after a rename. It moves to the new file at its own next build/reopen. This is accepted.\n\n### Reads\n\n- The serving connection to `random-cache.db` is read-only (`mode=ro` URI).\n- It needs no long busy wait, because nothing writes the active file in place.\n- Issue 32's 3600 s `RANDOM_CACHE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` wait and the `reuse_non_empty` keyword of `populate_random_cache` are retired or reworked, as plan.md lane 2d anticipates.\n- `fetch_random_rowids` and `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` keep their behaviour and signatures. The only change is that the connection they read may be replaced between calls.\n\n### Non-blocking startup (issue 23)\n\n- The Engine opens the existing cache if there is one, and starts listening without building first.\n- A refresh-on start runs its first build in the background worker. Refresh is on under the production default `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH = True` or with `--random-cache-refresh`.\n- A refresh-off start builds in the background only when the cache file is missing, or its `random_rowids` table is missing or empty. Refresh is off with `--dev` or `--no-random-cache-refresh`. Otherwise it serves the existing cache as it is.\n- Until a build has swapped in, a missing or empty cache is served through the existing DB fallback. That fallback is `fetch_random_rows` on the `[]` result from the cache, in `api/handlers/similar.py` `_fetch_random_rows` and the recommendation candidate sources, and it is unchanged.\n- `/api/health` must answer before the startup build completes.\n\n### Periodic refresh (issue 22)\n\n- A new setting `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` is read from the environment in `engine/server/api/server_config.py`. It is a non-negative integer, and 0 disables the periodic refresh.\n- When the variable is unset, the default is 60 minutes in production and 0 under `--dev`. An explicitly set value wins over `--dev`.\n- An invalid value (not an integer, or negative) exits at startup with a message naming the variable, like the existing `_resolve_*_env` helpers. `_resolve_positive_int_env` refuses 0, so this setting needs a non-negative variant.\n- `--no-random-cache-refresh` and `--random-cache-refresh` govern only the startup build, not the periodic one.\n- One daemon worker thread per Engine does all the building:\n  - It runs the startup build, if any, then one build every N minutes when N > 0.\n  - Two builds never run at once in one process.\n  - It stops on shutdown, and the Engine's shutdown is not delayed by an in-progress build.\n- With interval 0 and no startup build needed, no build runs.\n\n### Failure handling\n\n- A failed build (any exception during the scan, write, replace or reopen) deletes its temp file if present and leaves the active cache file and the serving connection untouched. It logs the failure reason and never raises into the request path.\n- A failed build is retried at the next interval tick.\n- Deliberate simplification: there is no separate backoff schedule and no max-build-runtime cap (issue 23's \"optional max build runtime\"). With interval 0, a failed startup build is not retried until the next restart. Upgrade path: add capped backoff in the worker loop if failures prove common.\n\n### Logs\n\nEach build logs:\n\n- duration\n- rows scanned\n- final size (valid candidates written)\n- the size target\n- filtered mode and the per-instance and per-author caps\n- when the fill comes up short, a line with target, got and scanned\n- the swap/reopen result, or on failure the reason\n\nThe log style follows the existing `logging.info` lines in `engine/server/data/random_cache.py` and `server.py`.\n\n### SQLite\n\n- There is no WAL. The active file is immutable between swaps and is read through a read-only connection.\n- The temp file is built in the default rollback-journal mode and fully closed before the rename, so no `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal` sidecar is left behind to be separated from its database by the rename.\n\n### Other writer\n\n- `engine/server/db/jobs/precompute-random-rowids.py` writes through the same temp-file plus `os.replace` path instead of writing `--out` in place. `scripts/run-dataset-build.sh` calls it.\n- Its CLI (`--db`, `--out`, `--size`, `--reset`, `--refresh`, `--filtered`, `--max-per-instance`, `--max-per-author`) and output are unchanged. `--reset` and `--refresh` keep their meaning of \"build fresh\" versus reuse when already at size.\n- A running Engine picks up a job-built cache at its next build/reopen or restart. The dataset build already says \"restart the Engine\".\n\n### Unchanged\n\n- The cache schema (`random_rowids(position, video_rowid)`) and contents semantics.\n- The filter semantics, `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_SIZE`, `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_FILTERED_MODE`, `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_MAX_PER_INSTANCE`, `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_MAX_PER_AUTHOR` and `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH`.\n- The random feed's output shape.\n- The test harness's `ENGINE_START_LOCK` serialisation and retry in `tests/active/conftest.py`.\n- Moving the cache to `ann_id` (plan 17 / issue 08) is out of scope.\n- The similarity cache is out of scope beyond keeping the swap helper reusable.\n\n### Acceptance\n\n- A refresh-on Engine start answers `/api/health` 200 before its startup build finishes.\n- Random-feed reads running concurrently with repeated build-and-swap cycles return no errors and no empty responses caused by the swap.\n- With a short interval, a periodic build swaps a new file in, and later random-feed reads are served from the new file.\n- With interval 0, no periodic build runs.\n- A failed build (forced) leaves the previous cache serving and its file intact, and removes its temp file.\n- An invalid `RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` exits at startup naming the variable. Unset gives 60, or 0 under `--dev`. An explicit value overrides `--dev`.\n- `precompute-random-rowids.py` produces the same cache contents as before, via temp file and replace.\n- `test_engines_starting_at_once_all_become_healthy` (8 Engines at once) still passes.\n- The issue-32 tests in `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` that assert the in-place rebuild contract are retired to `tests/archive` or rewritten for the new contract. These are the busy-wait tests `test_random_cache_connection_waits_longer_than_sqlite_default` and `test_rebuild_waits_for_a_write_lock_held_past_sqlite_default`, and the `reuse_non_empty` tests. The refresh-off reuse and missing/empty build behaviours keep test coverage.\n\n### Documentation to update\n\n- `DATA_BUILD.md` \u00a76 (in-place write and the one-hour wait statement).\n- `engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md` (the `DEFAULT_RANDOM_CACHE_REFRESH` entry and the new interval setting).\n- `DEPLOYMENT.md` where Engine env settings are listed.\n- Issues 22 and 23 are marked `complete` and moved to `docs/project/issues/archive/` on delivery.\n\n### Baseline suite state\n\nThe pre-build suite exited 0 (variant: false). Resolved paths: active tests `tests/active`, working `tests/tmp`, archive `tests/archive`, plans `docs/project/plans`, delete_me `delete_me`, record `tests/last_test_validation.json`, output `tests/last_test_output.txt`, project dir `/home/enduser/code/PeerTube-browser`.",
